title: On Agreing to the plan without argument
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：agree　|　正文 338 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 agree 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1972 the grandmother ① agreed to the plan without argument in silence, and every child in the courtyard said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the grandmother ② agrees to the plan without argument twice over without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ agree to the plan without argument at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ agreed to the plan without argument before — a line in the diary for February 1966 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Agreing to the plan without argument in silence, the grandmother said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the lamp at the far window, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ agree with the older record twice over, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Agree with the older record at once and never mention it again.

By 1979 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the diary, and a new child from the next courtyard ⑧ agrees with the older record in silence every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the window, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ agreed to the plan without argument again when nobody else would.

⑩ To agree to the plan without argument, my mother said in 1984, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the courtyard remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the courtyard forgets, somebody agrees to the plan without argument twice over again and somebody must agree to the plan without argument in silence all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 同意（一般过去式 agreed to the plan without argument：1972 年祖母头一回这样做，一言不发地）
B. v. 同意（一般现在 agrees to the plan without argument：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 同意（不定式 to agree to the plan without argument：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 同意（过去完成时 had agreed to the plan without argument：1966 年二月的日记上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 同意（动名词 agreing to the plan without argument 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 相符（agree with the older record：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去相符与更早的那条记载一致）
G. v. 相符（agree with the older record：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 同意（后段两处：新来的孩子照例 agrees with the older record，而母亲又一次 agreed to the plan without argument）

answers.why: agree 意为“同意”，1972 年祖母一言不发地同意二话不说答应了那个计划，那是院子里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 agreed。
agree 意为“同意”，自那以后祖母来回两遍把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 agrees。
agree 意为“同意”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯同意二话不说答应了那个计划”，此处为不定式 to agree to the plan without argument。
agree 意为“同意”，日记里 二月 那行字说明早在 1979 年之前就有人同意过，故用过去完成时 had agreed。
agree 意为“同意”，祖母说“同意二话不说答应了那个计划这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 agreing to the plan without argument 作主语。
agree 意为“相符”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去相符与更早的那条记载一致”，should ever 之后用原形 agree with the older record。
agree 意为“相符”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻相符与更早的那条记载一致（agree with the older record at once），以后再也不要提起。
agree 意为“同意”，新来的孩子每个年头都照例相符与更早的那条记载一致，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 agrees。
agree 意为“同意”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次一言不发地同意二话不说答应了那个计划，用一般过去式 agreed 叙述。
agree 意为“同意”，结尾那句是母亲 1984 年的话：要同意二话不说答应了那个计划，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和院子记住的那一件。

多年以后，祖母仍来回两遍做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（agrees to the plan without argument）
母亲后来说，难就难在肯同意二话不说答应了那个计划这件事本身。（to agree to the plan without argument）
早在 1966 年就有人同意二话不说答应了那个计划，二月那天日记上的一行字就是证据。（had agreed to the plan without argument）
祖母说过，一言不发地同意二话不说答应了那个计划这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（agreing to the plan without argument 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻相符与更早的那条记载一致，以后再也不要提起。（agree with the older record，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 agree 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1972 the grandmother agreed to the plan without argument in silence, and nobody in the courtyard forgot it.
Even now the grandmother agrees to the plan without argument twice over whenever the courtyard asks.
Agreing to the plan without argument in silence, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever agree with the older record twice over, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new child from the next courtyard agrees with the older record in silence every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother agreed to the plan without argument again, and the courtyard remembered that half.
